name: Government of Brazil
role: Federal government (Lula administration); Finance Minister Fernando Haddad co-led the proposals below
notes: Its G20 presidency in 2024 put a minimum tax on billionaires on the G20 agenda.

name: Government of Spain
role: Government of Spain; ministers María Jesús Montero and Carlos Cuerpo co-led the proposals below
notes: Spain also levies the Impuesto Temporal de Solidaridad de las Grandes Fortunas (Ley 38/2022), recorded in the Spanish register under the Cortes Generales (es-A0060).

name: Government of South Africa
role: National Treasury under Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana
notes: Co-signed the 2024 global billionaire levy article, then rejected a domestic wealth tax in a parliamentary reply (May 2025). The latest evidence is the rejection, so no seat is lit; a position on a coordinated global minimum is not established.

name: Government of Colombia
role: Government of President Gustavo Petro, in office until 7 August 2026
notes: Petro's term ended on 7 August 2026. His successor, Abelardo de la Espriella, said in his inauguration speech that the wealth tax will be eliminated (Publimetro, 2026-08-07); the seat stays dark while he is in office.

name: Government of Argentina
notes: The Fernández government's one-off levy on large fortunes (Ley 27.605, 2020). President Milei, in office since December 2023, opposes it; the seat stays dark.

name: Government of Bolivia
notes: The Arce government's Impuesto a las Grandes Fortunas (Ley 1357, 2020). Arce left office in November 2025; whether the tax is still in force has not been checked.

name: Government of Norway
role: Government of Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre (Labour)
notes: Keeps and adjusts the long-standing net wealth tax (formuesskatt). Its own budget pages (regjeringen.no) sit behind a bot check; the evidence is the budget as reported and the governing party's campaign position.

name: Government of Chile
notes: The wealth tax was part of the Boric government's 2022 tax reform bill, which the Chamber of Deputies is reported to have rejected in March 2023. Boric left office in March 2026.

name: Government of Cuba
role: Government of Cuba; Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla addressing the UN General Assembly
notes: A call at the UN for a tax on billionaires; Cuba has no wealth tax of its own that this register knows of.
